title: Internal: handling procedure for waking a dormant Savings & Money Market Accounts account and moving it up a money market tier
content:
## When this procedure applies

This procedure applies to a dormant Savings & Money Market Accounts account whose identity-verified owner, in one contact on a business day (Monday through Friday, other than a Federal Reserve holiday), moves certificate of deposit money out of it by telephone transfer to their own checking account and asks to move the account up to the highest-ranked money market tier they qualify for. The owner's transfer is the customer-initiated transaction that reactivates the account, any maintenance fee owed back on the account is refunded, and the conversion is decided on the corrected balance.

When the procedure is complete, the account is active with the posted date of the owner's transfer, which is the day of the contact, as its latest customer-initiated activity, carries the refund credit and the transfer, and holds the target tier, or keeps its tier when no higher tier qualifies.

## Steps

1. **Owner's transfer of certificate money.** transfer_savings_to_checking_5f60835b, performed by the customer themselves. This is the owner-instructed transfer of certificate money that reactivates the account; its amount is the one the certificate-money transfer policy sets.
2. **Reactivation.** reactivate_savings_account_bfe70db1, performed by the agent. The reactivation is dated by the owner's transfer: the posted date of the step 1 withdrawal is given as the reactivation date, as the same-contact reactivation policy decides it.
3. **Maintenance fee refund.** refund_savings_maintenance_fee_bf99bb2f, performed by the agent. This is the bank-error refund of the maintenance fee under the waivers of the general maintenance-fee rules.
4. **Tier conversion.** convert_savings_tier_d500151b, performed by the agent. This is the conversion to the highest qualifying money market tier, as the money market upgrade policy decides it.

## Who does what

| Step | Performed by | Posts or changes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the customer themselves | a withdrawal on the savings account |
| 2 | agent | the account's status and latest-activity date |
| 3 | agent | a refund credit on the savings account |
| 4 | agent | the account's tier |

## What flows from one step to the next

- Step 1 to step 2: the posted date of the owner's withdrawal becomes the reactivation date passed in step 2.
- Step 2 to step 4: the active status set in step 2 is what satisfies the requirement that the account be active when the conversion is recorded.

## Why the steps are in this order

- **Transfer before reactivation.** The dormancy rules require a customer-initiated transaction in the same contact to reactivate a dormant account, and make that transaction's date the new latest-activity date. Reactivating first would leave no transaction and no date to record.
- **Reactivation directly after the transfer.** The reactivation comes directly after the transaction that justifies it, because the dormancy rules tie it to that transaction in the same contact.
- **Refund third.** The fee refund and the reactivation change different records and commute, so no policy outcome depends on their relative order; the procedure places the refund third only so that it has one fixed sequence.
- **Refund before conversion.** The upgrade policy compares the balance after every refund owed on the account has posted with each tier's minimum opening deposit. Converting first would test the uncorrected balance.
- **Reactivation before conversion.** The tier conversion rules require the account to be active when the conversion is recorded.

Every step is a synchronous posting or status change completed at the same moment of the contact; none waits for an outside event or for time to pass. On a business day the owner's transfer and the refund post on the day of the contact. On a Saturday, Sunday or Federal Reserve holiday the transfer would post only on the next business day, so the same-contact reactivation policy establishes no reactivation date and this procedure does not apply.

## If two adjacent steps were swapped

Swapping steps 2 and 3 changes no policy outcome, because the reactivation and the refund commute. The other swaps would go wrong as follows.

| Swap | What would go wrong |
|---|---|
| step 2 before step 1 | no customer-initiated transaction and no date exist to reactivate on |
| step 4 before step 3 | the target tier would be chosen on the balance before the refund |
